question: With the SESSION-LEVEL MCP lock removed, does per-agent AgentDefinition.disallowedTools: ['mcp__*'] remove the child's MCP tools on its own — or is production's second layer a no-op that probe G could not distinguish from a boundary?
whyThisExists: Probe G's narrowed arm ran with initMcpServerCount=0 and initMcpToolNames=[], so the per-agent spec removed tools that were ALREADY ABSENT. Its PASS is fully explained by the session-level lock alone. This probe is the arm that separates 'the mechanism held' from 'the mechanism was never invoked'.
comparisonBaseline: Probe G's UNNARROWED arm, same prompt, same target agent, same instrument, 2026-07-28: child = 619 names of which 588 mcp__, with a child-originated mcp__github__get_me observed. That is what a child looks like when nothing removes MCP.

mcpControlFile.note: NO CENSUS FILE. Nothing was measured through this channel.

notes: MEASURED: AgentDefinition.disallowedTools:["mcp__*"] DOES NOT bind on its own in SDK 0.3.220. The child still shows an MCP surface: census mcp__ names=589, stated MCP_TOTAL=n/a, mcpAttemptObserved=false, evidence={"preToolUseFiringsInsideSubagentForMcp":[],"mcpNamesInChildTranscript":[]}. Probe G's PASS therefore rests ENTIRELY on the session-level lock, and the per-agent spec that claude-builder.ts calls defence in depth is decoration. This is a finding, not an apparatus failure: the control held.
caveats: The session hit the 300s ceiling. The child writes before the parent, so the census survives; the parent's MCP control file may not, and the control gate reads the engine-side init channel as well for exactly that reason.
n=1. One live session, one model, one target agent (trigger-dev-expert, chosen because it carries no `tools:` frontmatter allowlist).

postRunAudit.addedAt: 2026-07-28, after the run, by a script that ADDS this key and changes no measured value
postRunAudit.whichChannelCarriesTheFinding: ENUMERATION, not reachability. The session hit the 300s ceiling after the child's Write, so the child never reached its step-2 MCP call and SubagentStop never fired (no child transcript). mcpAttemptObserved=false therefore means 'not attempted in the time available', NOT 'blocked'. The FAIL rests on the child having ENUMERATED 589 concrete mcp__ tool names while its AgentDefinition carried disallowedTools:['mcp__*']. No MCP tool name appears in any prompt (assertPromptNamesNoMcpTool enforces it at run time), so the child can only have read those names off its own tool schema.
postRunAudit.decisiveCrossCheck: The G2 child's mcp__ set is IDENTICAL to probe G's UNNARROWED child's mcp__ set except for one name (mcp__trigger__update_prompt_override, extra in G2 - G2's session loaded 22 servers, G's 13), and their non-mcp names are identical. Artefacts: probes/results/raw/G-PERAGENT-census-child.txt vs probes/results/raw/G-census-unnarrowed-child.txt. A spec documented to 'remove all MCP tools' removed nothing observable.
postRunAudit.truncationBias: The census carries no TOTAL=/MCP_TOTAL= trailer (the run was cut off), so it may be missing a tail. Truncation can only LOWER the mcp count, i.e. it biases AGAINST this FAIL. 589 is a floor.
postRunAudit.controlThatHeld: The parent's MCP control file was never written (same ceiling), so the control rests on the engine-side channel: system/init reported 22 MCP servers and 9 mcp__ names already in init.tools. The gate was built to accept either channel for exactly this reason.
postRunAudit.serverCountNondeterminism: 22 servers here vs 13 in probe G under comparable options - the README's standing caveat. Only 0-vs-nonzero is a sound signal; nothing here compares counts across runs.
postRunAudit.whatThisDoesNotSay: It does not say disallowedTools is inert for every value or every tool - only that the server-level spec 'mcp__*' did not remove MCP tools from this child in SDK 0.3.220. n=1.

twoReadingsOfThisFAIL.reading_a: AgentDefinition.disallowedTools:['mcp__*'] is inert for MCP server-level specs in SDK 0.3.220.
twoReadingsOfThisFAIL.reading_b: Options.agents does not bind at all for a SAME-NAMED on-disk agent (merge-vs-replace, flagged UNMEASURED in agent-shortlist.ts). Then maxTurns, background:false AND disallowedTools are all inert for the 141 shortlisted agents that exist on disk - a strictly larger finding.
twoReadingsOfThisFAIL.whyNotSeparatedHere: Checked and unavailable: neither the child's ...subagents/agent-*.jsonl nor the parent session transcript stores a system prompt, so the probe-supplied AgentDefinition.prompt cannot be distinguished from the disk agent's prose in either file (searched both for a distinctive phrase from each; zero hits for both). init.agents carries names only, and the name exists in both sources.
twoReadingsOfThisFAIL.howToSeparate_oneSession: Put a unique nonce in AgentDefinition.prompt and ask the child to echo it. Echoed -> the definition bound and reading (a) stands. Absent -> reading (b), and every per-agent bound in claude-builder.ts is decoration for on-disk agents. Not spent here: the session budget for this task was 4 and 3 were used.
twoReadingsOfThisFAIL.sharedConsequence: Under BOTH readings the production claim is the same: the child's MCP surface is held by managedSettings.allowedMcpServers:[] + allowManagedMcpServersOnly ALONE. There is no working second layer behind it.
